Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2, 2019

Published July 12, 2019

As of 2024-03-01 this post has been viewed 500,000 times.

On Tuesday, July 2, 2019 Cloudflare experienced a major global outage affecting all our customers for 27 minutes. A newly deployed WAF rule contained a regular expression with catastrophic backtracking behavior. The rule was evaluated on every CPU, worldwide, and drove CPU utilization to 100% across our L7 stack.

Our WAF rules had no per-operation CPU time budget, and the deployment pipeline performed syntactic validation only — there was no performance regression test, so a pathological regex could slip into production and reach 100% of traffic in minutes.

The fault was triggered by a global WAF rule push. Because the push is a single deployment event reaching every data center simultaneously, the blast radius was global. We have since split WAF rule deployments into a canary phase followed by a staged rollout, and CPU-time budgets are enforced on every regex evaluation.

During those 27 minutes HTTP 502 responses spiked globally, and request volume dropped to near zero. We believe the incident affected routing of Cloudflare CDN traffic through roughly 90% of our edge network.

RFC 9110 defines the 502 Bad Gateway status code; our routing layer returned 502 because the origin connections could not complete within the configured timeout. This outage is not associated with any CVE.
